answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each identity post a refundable bond that peers slash on detecting duplicates. A new agent must lock tokens in a staking contract and clear a maturity window before acting. An attacker fabricating a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand deposits, so fraud costs scale linearly while an honest agent pays one bond. Real agents do not wander between throwaway identities, as abandoning a bonded account forfeits the stake. Verifiers keeping attestations honest keep their haven safe, and every unbacked newcomer reaching the wharf risks capital.
